relatedSnapshot.title: Adding leads to an existing campaign wipes the campaign's existing leads while still consuming credits
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Name 5 signal (daily triage 2026-07-29)

Name 5 cluster *Campaign leads vanish after new upload, credits consumed* — severity high, confidence 0.88, **2 customers this week**.

* **Name 3 (Company One)**: 5,347 existing leads in a campaign disappeared when she added more leads to it.
* **Name 4**: hit the same data-loss pattern today.

In both cases the leads are gone and the credits were still charged, so the customer pays twice to rebuild the list.

Name 5 topic: <url>

## Why this is a new issue

Duplicate search found no open canonical for "adding leads wipes the existing lead set":

* ENG-10981 "Scraped leads disappear after processing — credits consumed, campaign stays empty" — Done (2026-06-29); different trigger (initial scrape, not a second upload into a populated campaign)
* ENG-8186 "Cold Email Agent lead count resets after import" — Done (2026-05-03)
* ENG-7942 "Campaign upload loses leads and skips to step 4" — Done
* ENG-4551 "Missing ~760 leads after CSV import" — Done
* ENG-7247 / ENG-7186 — deletion/duplicate-skip behaviour, not data loss on add

Distinct from the stuck-processing cluster on ENG-10762: here the leads were present and are afterwards gone.

## Suggested starting points

* The add-leads path into an existing campaign: whether the import replaces rather than appends the campaign lead set
* Credit deduction on the second import happening before/independently of the lead write, so credits are consumed even when the resulting lead set shrinks

* Name 6 key: `modem_daily_triage:v1/<uuid>/2026-07-29`
* Window: 2026-07-28 13:02 UTC → 2026-07-29 13:02 UTC

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: purchased campaign leads hard-deleted by automatic completed-campaign cleanup, campaign shows 0 leads while History still reports the uploads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>
Contact: Name 3, Company One Workspace. The Intercom source URL points directly at the campaign in view: "Management Consulting | Name 7 | May 2026".

## Conversation context (bounded)

The customer reports that 5,000 leads purchased for that campaign went missing, that the total is now 7,802, and that it has been over a month without resolution. She says the Leads tab History view shows uploads while the campaign table shows 0 leads, and that she did not delete them: "when I purchased more leads the first time there was an issue the first 5000 disappeared, I purchased 1500 more and now they are also gone." She asks whether a record of the purchased leads exists, then asked for a human agent. Fin AI replied with the History view and deletion-recovery guidance; no human has answered.

## Claim

Leads purchased for a cold email campaign are hard-deleted from that campaign by the platform's automatic completed-campaign lead removal, which a later lead purchase triggers when the workspace is short on provider lead space, so the campaign ends up with 0 leads while its Leads tab History still reports every purchase as uploaded.

## Evidence

* Production: the campaign holds 0 lead rows (including soft-deleted); its Leads tab History holds 18 lead sources totalling 7,969 leads recorded as uploaded.
* Production activity log: "Deleted all 5686 leads from campaign" at 2026-07-27T17:03:04Z and "Deleted all 2630 leads from campaign" at 2026-10-02T18:19:05Z, both on this campaign.
* Name 8: Inngest run 01M3YXDZ55D5P0723AXMDM7EW1 (ai-clients.campaigns.process-delete-all-leads, COMPLETED 2026-10-02T18:19:06Z) returned deletedFromDb 2630, providerDeletedCount 2531; its step trace contains classify-final-capacity-plan, a step that only runs on the automatic-completed-campaign-cleanup branch. The deletion followed a lead purchase for a different campaign by 23 seconds.
* Code: process-lead-generator.ts sends PROCESS_LEAD_REMOVAL when provider lead space is low; process-lead-removal.ts fans out campaign-delete-all-leads with deletionSource automatic_completed_campaign_cleanup for every Completed campaign; process-campaign-delete-all-leads.ts deletes at the provider then calls deleteAllLeadsByCampaign (hard delete, all rows, no recency guard).
* Blast radius (queried 2026-10-05): 727 "Deleted all N leads from campaign" activity rows across 245 organizations in the last 30 days, 221 of them within 15 minutes after a lead purchase for the same organization; 3,032 campaigns currently in Completed status still holding live leads across 1,416 organizations.
* Related open work: ENG-12122 (this same customer and campaign, 5,347 leads reported lost on 2026-07-29, Urgent, Blocked) and ENG-11215 (sibling automatic cleanup hard-deleting campaign lead lists, Backlog).

relatedSnapshot.title: Support: cold email campaign lead list wiped by a permanent Delete All, not restorable
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Intercom source

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Conversation context (bounded)

Customer (workspace <workspace-slug>, slug <workspace-slug>) reported that a lead list created the previous day was "no longer loaded" and said they thought they had deleted it by mistake. They added: it was a list they "used credit for", created "around 11:30", in the campaign "Manufacturer - New Name 9", roughly 10K leads, and "it was automatically done when setting up the campaign". Support asked how many leads were scraped and whether they were uploaded.

## Testable claim

A customer's lead list for the cold email campaign "Manufacturer - New Name 9" was wiped on 2026-09-14 at 16:30 local (20:30 UTC) by an explicit delete-all-leads action, which permanently removes lead records from both Acquisity and the sending provider, and the list cannot be restored from inside the product.

## What the evidence shows

1. Campaign "Manufacturer - New Name 9" still exists (paused), wizard completed and launched 2026-09-14 14:43 local, total_leads field still reads 7,335, but it now holds zero lead records.
2. 48 provider upload receipts between 12:23 and 15:59 local on 2026-09-14 record 21,457 leads uploaded to the campaign. The wizard's AI Lead Search for the campaign ran 11:52-12:30 local (7,335 requested, 3,911 leads delivered).
3. At 16:30:43 local the campaign activity records "Deleted all 21465 leads from campaign", followed by a provider delete receipt for 21,457 leads and an Inngest run output of {deletedFromDb: 0, providerDeletedCount: 21457}. The local lead rows were deleted first and the provider cleanup was queued immediately after, which is the signature of the in-app delete-all path (or the workflow step that calls the same mutation), not of the automatic completed-campaign cleanup. That automatic path is ruled out: it only targets completed campaigns, does not delete from the provider, and touches the database after the provider, not before.
4. The deletion is hard, not soft: no live or soft-deleted lead rows remain for this organization from after 2025-12-17. Product documentation states Delete All is permanent and the confirmation dialog names the exact lead count before it runs.
5. The underlying AI Lead Search results are still stored at workspace level (3,911 scraped leads under the campaign's lead-source record), so the searched population survives even though the campaign list is gone.
6. The conversation included one customer screenshot ("this is the search I did") that could not be interpreted in this pass; it is listed as an unread evidence lane, not as evidence.

## Verdict

User action, permanent by design. Nothing in the evidence indicates an internal failure: the lead set was removed by an explicit delete-all operation, the customer's own account is that they deleted it by mistake, and there is no restore path for campaign leads in the product.

## Unblock

Rebuild the list rather than restore it: re-import the original CSV (no lead credits) and/or re-run the AI Lead Search for the same niche and filters (consumes lead credits). Export leads before any future deletion.

## Open human decision

Whether the lead credits spent on the deleted search warrant a goodwill credit is a commercial call, not an engineering one. Please settle it with the customer directly.

## Reopen condition

Reopen toward a product defect only if the delete-all operation is shown to have been triggered without the customer acting: for example, by a workflow or automated actor on this workspace rather than the in-app control.

relatedSnapshot.title: Prevent duplicate leads by phone number and improve merge rules
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The CRM can partially prevent duplicates today, but deduplication is still limited and does not reliably stop duplicate lead or contact creation when the same phone number already exists in the workspace.

This creates duplicate records across lead creation flows, makes merge decisions more manual than they should be, and increases the risk of splitting conversation history, deals, and activity across multiple records.

Current gaps:

* Duplicate prevention is not consistently enforced for phone numbers.
* Existing deduplication appears to focus more on email-based matching than phone-based matching.
* Duplicate checks are not guaranteed to behave the same way across manual creation, imports, messaging sync, and automation flows.
* Merge guidance is not strong enough when records partially match and need safe reconciliation.
* Merging duplicates must preserve related threads, deals, and activity so no context is lost.

## Solution

Build workspace-wide phone-number deduplication for leads and contacts, and strengthen merge behavior so duplicate records can be identified and reconciled safely.

Scope of work:

* Add duplicate detection based on phone number, not just email.
* Normalize phone numbers before matching so equivalent formats are treated as the same value.
* Enforce the same duplicate-checking behavior across:
  * manual record creation
  * imports
  * messaging sync
  * automation-based creation paths
* Define the expected system behavior when a duplicate phone number is detected:
  * block creating a net-new record when there is an exact match
  * surface the existing matching record to the user or workflow
  * route partial or ambiguous matches into merge suggestions instead of silently creating duplicates
* Improve merge suggestions and merge rules so users can safely review and reconcile likely duplicates when records are not exact matches.
* Ensure merge operations preserve and reattach related data correctly, including:
  * threads
  * deals
  * activity history

Implementation should make duplicate prevention and merge behavior consistent regardless of entry point, while preserving data continuity when records are merged.

relatedSnapshot.title: CSV uploads with email verification show misleading "Lead Scraping" status
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue Identified:

Cold Email Agent triggers lead-scrape flow on manual CSV uploads with verification enabled

When a user uploads a CSV file to an existing campaign with **“Lead emails will be automatically verified”** toggled on, the Cold Email Agent incorrectly enters the **lead-scraping** process (shows “Collecting leads from source”).

### Current Behavior

The UI gets stuck showing:

* "Lead Scraping - Collecting leads from source" (<stripe-id>)

### Expected behavior

Manual uploads should bypass scraping entirely — the system should verify the uploaded leads, then add them to **Manual Uploads**, without invoking the lead-scrape flow.

For CSV uploads with email verification enabled:

* Should NOT show "Lead Scraping" status as in-progress
* Should skip directly to "Email Verification" status, OR
* Should immediately mark scraping as "completed" since no scraping is needed

## Customer Name 11

* Name: Name 10
* Campaign: Venture Capital & Private Equity | CEO, Chief Executive Officer, Founder, Co-founder, Owner | 51-100 | United States
* Screenshot: 

 <image> 

---

## Root Cause

In `trpc/routers/outreach/leads.ts` (lines 654-735), when `isEmailVerificationEnabled` is true, the code calls `convertCsvLeadsToScrapeFormatForBulkUploadAndEmailVerification()` which creates a `LeadScrapeRun` with `status: LeadScrapeRunStatus.Running` (line 202 in `lib/scrape/db.ts`).

This causes the UI component `LeadSourceStatus` to display the scraping stage as "<stripe-id>" with the description "Collecting leads from source".

## Files Involved

* `trpc/routers/outreach/leads.ts` (lines 654-735)
* `lib/scrape/db.ts` (line 152-220, specifically line 202)
* `components/lead-sources/lead-source-status.tsx` (UI component)

## Suggested Fix

Option 1: Set scrape status to "completed" immediately for CSV uploads

```typescript
status: LeadScrapeRunStatus.Completed, // instead of Running
```

Option 2: Create a different submission type that skips the scraping stage entirely

## Additional Context

* "Add Leads" option is toggled OFF in campaign options
* This affects the Cold Email Agent workflow for CSV uploads

relatedSnapshot.title: Attach transferred Twilio numbers to a workspace
relatedSnapshot.description:
> **Audit update (2026-09-01; verified against origin/main** `b56300e23152`**):** The native Name 12 status and blocker relations now reflect the verified current scope. Existing description history is preserved below.

> ## 🕒 DEFERRED, not needed for the migration (decided 2026-08-03)
>
> **James's call: reps get brand new numbers. We are not moving the existing Close numbers across.** That removes this ticket from the migration entirely, so it is dropped to Low and parked.
>
> Keeping it open because it is a genuine product capability: any customer moving to us from another CRM will want to keep their numbers, and the research below (how the transfer works, what breaks, what order to do it in) is the expensive part and is already done.
>
> **One accepted consequence worth remembering:** leads text and call reps for months after the last conversation. Name 13 still gets texts from leads he last spoke to four months ago. Those messages will keep arriving at the old Close numbers and nobody will see them. If that matters later, the mitigation is to keep Close's inbox monitored for a while after the move, or set up forwarding, rather than to revive this ticket.

> **Context.** Glossary: master ticket ENG-12250. For THIS ticket: "porting" means moving an existing phone number from one provider to another so it keeps working and keeps its history, instead of the rep getting a brand new number. Name 13 wants this: *"I personally still get texts from leads and haven't closed for 4 months+. It's better to keep one."* Why it matters: prospects text and call reps months after the last conversation. A new number silently loses all of that, and nobody notices, because the messages simply never arrive.

**Size:** M · **Design:** none · Blocked by: ENG-12263 **· MVP****
****How it should work (Close reference): **<url>

### Overview

After this ticket, a number moved across from Close can be added to a workspace and assigned to a rep, and it works for calls and texts exactly like a number we bought.

### Problem

The purchase flow assumes we are buying a brand new number from the provider's stock. A ported number arrives at our provider account by a different route, as an operational process, and there is no way to bring one into a workspace afterwards.

**Good news on the operational side.** Close runs on Twilio and so do we, so this is an **internal transfer between two Twilio accounts**, not a carrier port. Close's own documentation calls that path "greatly simplified": you email their support saying you are moving to another Twilio subaccount, they approve and send their account id, and both sides file a matching internal-transfer ticket with Twilio. Days, not the two-to-four weeks a carrier port needs (which requires a signed authorisation form, a copy of the losing carrier's invoice, and exact name and address matching).

So the numbers may arrive sooner than expected, which makes this ticket more urgent rather than less. What we need in code is the ability to attach a number that already exists to a workspace and a rep, and to make sure everything it needs is set up.

### Solution

* Add a way for a platform admin to attach an existing number to a workspace and a rep.
* Make sure it gets everything a bought number gets: the correct webhook addresses so calls and texts reach us, capabilities recorded correctly, and attachment to the approved messaging service.
* Document the operational steps in the ticket so whoever runs the port knows the order: request the port, wait for it to complete, attach the number, then verify a real call and a real text before telling the rep to use it.
* Handle the in-between period. During a port the number can stop working for a short window, so schedule it and tell the rep in advance.

### Scope

* In: attaching an existing number, its setup, verification steps, the written operational runbook.
* Out of scope: automating the port request itself with the provider, which is a manual process on their side.

### Acceptance criteria

1. A platform admin can attach an existing number to a workspace and assign it to a rep.
2. An attached number receives calls and texts, and both appear against the right rep.
3. It is attached to the approved messaging service, like a bought number.
4. The runbook is written and has been followed once, end to end, for one real number.

### ⚠️ Transferred numbers arrive with NO configuration. Read this before scheduling anything.

Twilio's documentation is explicit: *"Twilio numbers lose their existing configuration when transferred between accounts as well as any messaging settings such as opt-outs and A2P registrations. You will need to reconfigure, setup Opt-Outs and re-register the numbers on the new account before they will work."*

What that means in practice:

* **There is no carrier downtime.** The number never leaves Twilio's network, so unlike a real port there is no cutover window where the number stops existing.
* **But it arrives dead.** No voice webhook, no messaging webhook, no A2P registration, no opt-out list. Calls and texts fail until we configure it. **The length of that outage is entirely under our control**, which is what makes this ticket the difference between minutes and days.
* **Voice comes back in minutes** once the webhooks are set, which is the core of this ticket.
* **Texting depends on A2P**, and the sending team's existing registration does not transfer. The number must be attached to an approved messaging service on the receiving account. If the receiving workspace already has an approved brand, that is an API call. **If it does not, texting stays down until brand and campaign vetting completes**, which is the long pole and can take days.

**Required order of operations, and it is not the obvious one:**

1. Register the receiving workspace's A2P brand and campaign FIRST, using the registration flow that shipped with ENG-8475. This is the long pole.
2. Only once it is approved, request the number transfer.
3. Have this ticket's work ready so numbers are configured the moment they land.

Transfer before the brand is approved and the numbers arrive unable to send a single text.

Also note: Twilio only self-serves transfers between an account and **its own** subaccounts. A transfer from an unrelated account is a **support ticket filed by both sides**, not an API call (Twilio error 21473 if attempted directly).

Reference: <url>

### Note

⚠️ The request side is owned by James and is in flight. Decide which Twilio account the numbers should land in before filing, and see (ENG-8475, Twilio A2P subaccount SMS). **That ticket's code merged on 2026-07-26 (PR #3850, commit** `4f01503f1a`) and the ticket description is stale. The `twilio_subaccount` table, the registration wizard, and subaccount-aware number purchase are all live on main. What remains is operational: an approved Twilio ISV primary customer profile, the `TWILIO_PRIMARY_CUSTOMER_PROFILE_SID` and `PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env vars set in production (both are optional in code, so they fail at call time rather than at boot), and one real end-to-end registration run.

Strong recommendation: give the sales workspace **its own subaccount and A2P brand** rather than landing these numbers on the shared platform brand. At 3,500 to 5,000 texts a day on a shared brand, a carrier flag takes SMS down for every client at once, and any other client's behaviour can take the sales team's texting down mid-migration.

Reference: <url> see "Porting numbers out of Close".

relatedSnapshot.title: Protect manually uploaded leads through dispatch, re-upload and sync
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Leads a rep uploads by CSV or adds by hand lose their "manual" label after they are sent to the provider, get re-sent when uploaded again, and can be deleted by a later sync before the provider ever received them.

## Problem

Three related bugs in the manual lead lifecycle:

1. **"Manual" label wiped after dispatch.** After a dispatch page completes, the code sets each lead's `source` to an empty string as a marker. Production sample: 4,832 of 6,873 campaign leads have an empty source and only 7 are marked manual. The campaign agent's CSV guard counts manual leads to decide whether a CSV-only campaign has targeting; with the label gone the guard never blocks, so the agent can scrape more leads for a CSV-only campaign without targeting. Deleting a single manual lead also filters on the manual label, so it leaves the workspace lead row behind.
2. **Re-uploading existing leads resets them.** When a CSV contains emails already in the campaign, the upsert sets `source` back to manual and gives them a new batch id without checking whether they were already dispatched or soft-deleted. They are pushed to the provider again, counted as new in upload totals, and soft-deleted rows are counted as linked.
3. **Unsent manual leads deleted by sync.** The full import deletes campaign leads that do not carry the current provider campaign id once they are older than 24 hours. Manual and scraped leads are only stamped with that id by the import, so leads still waiting to be sent after 24 hours (for example blocked by lead capacity) are permanently deleted.

## User experience

A rep uploads a CSV. The campaign keeps knowing those leads were manual, re-uploading the same people does not send them again, and leads waiting to be sent are never deleted by a sync.

## Proposed fix

Use a dedicated dispatch state instead of blanking `source`, make re-uploads leave dispatched and deleted leads alone, and only let the mismatch cleanup delete leads the provider is known to have had.

## What's included

* A dispatch marker that does not touch `source`, plus a backfill that restores the manual label where it can be derived (for example from manual batch ids).
* Re-upload skips leads already dispatched or soft-deleted and reports them separately in upload counts.
* The mismatch cleanup only deletes leads that were stamped for another provider campaign or that the provider previously returned.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## Done when

- [ ] After dispatch, manual leads still count as manual and the CSV guard blocks a CSV-only campaign without targeting.
- [ ] Re-uploading an already dispatched lead does not push it to the provider again.
- [ ] A manual lead older than 24 hours that was not yet sent survives a full import.

## Implementation context

Measured on 17 September 2026 from read-only production samples (0.01% to 0.05% of each table, so treat sizes as plus or minus 20%) and code at origin/main c51db1d4e6. Related: Master: Company Two lead-push page-dispatch job fails and Campaign lead lists hard-deleted by automated orphaned-campaign cleanup. Code paths and evidence are in AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Leads Contacted card shows a lifetime provider count and can exceed Leads Uploaded after a lead list is replaced
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: a workspace owner (workspace "Name 14's Workspace") reports two cold email campaigns as technical faults. "Health & Supplements Manufacturing | Leadership | US | Name 7 (AIA Created)" shows 5,400 leads contacted against 2,955 uploaded; their screenshot of the campaign's Leads tab reads Leads Uploaded 2,955, Leads Contacted 5,400, Leads In Progress 5,281. "Funding | Leadership | US | Name 7 (AIA Created)" shows 294 contacted and no replies. They also report a high number of bounced emails.

Finding: the two figures count different populations. "Leads Contacted" is the outreach provider's lifetime count of unique leads that ever received an email on that campaign (5,400), while "Leads Uploaded" is the leads currently on the campaign (2,955, all added on 14 Sep). The campaign has been sending since 8 July and its lead list has been replaced and trimmed since: provider upload receipts alone record 695 leads accepted on 31 Aug and 2,950 on 14 Sep, and 5,295 campaign-completed-without-reply events exist for this campaign. "Leads In Progress" (5,281) inherits the same mismatch.

The help centre article for the Analytics tab states the Leads Contacted number is capped at total leads uploaded and "can never exceed it". On this campaign it does, so the documented behaviour and the card disagree once a lead list has been replaced.

Sending is unaffected and no customer action is needed for sending to work. The open product question is whether the card should cap or relabel the contacted figure, or the article should describe its lifetime scope.

Reopen if the customer confirms they never removed or replaced the campaign's leads, which would make the count a data defect rather than a scope mismatch.

relatedSnapshot.title: Automatically Create and Link CRM Companies
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Automatically create or reuse the correct CRM company from persisted campaign lead data, then link it to the synced contact and deal.

This removes manual company cleanup without using conversation analysis or guessing between ambiguous companies.

## Delivery order

**Name 17 programme ticket.**

* **Blocked by:** ENG-12420 - Make Contact and Deal Updates Atomic, ENG-12422 - Handle Uncommon CRM Stages Deterministically, ENG-12423 - Remove Legacy CRM Model Calls and ENG-12428 - Store and Show CRM Company Employee Ranges.
* **Assignment:** Unassigned.

## What to build

Resolve a company candidate from persisted campaign lead data using this precedence:

1. Explicit user corrections or overrides.
2. Persisted campaign lead metadata and custom fields.
3. Linked lead-scrape data.
4. No conversation-derived or inferred contact fallback.

Conservative company matching:

1. Reuse one active company in the same organisation when there is one unique exact normalized domain or website match.
2. If no domain match exists, reuse one unique exact normalized company-name match.
3. If multiple matches exist, skip and record an ambiguous result.
4. If no match exists and a valid company name is available, create the company.
5. Do not use fuzzy matching.
6. Derive an email domain only from a non-public corporate email and only when a valid company name exists.

Create or reuse the company within the deterministic transaction, then link it to the contact and deal. Reprocessing and concurrent delivery must not create duplicate companies or links.

Populate only supported empty fields:

* Company name.
* Name 18 or domain.
* Description.
* Industry.
* Exact employee count when available.
* Employee-size range from ENG-12428 when available.

Preserve stronger user-entered values. Missing or ambiguous company data is a non-blocking no-op with telemetry. Unexpected database failures roll back and retry rather than leaving half-created records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A campaign lead with a valid company candidate creates or reuses one company.
- [ ] The same company is linked to the CRM contact and deal.
- [ ] Exact domain matching is organisation-scoped and unique.
- [ ] Exact normalized name matching is used only when there is one unique result.
- [ ] Ambiguous matches are skipped and never guessed.
- [ ] Public email domains are never used as company domains.
- [ ] Exact employee counts and employee-size ranges are preserved separately.
- [ ] Existing manual company fields are not overwritten by weaker source data.
- [ ] Duplicate and concurrent processing creates one company and one set of links.
- [ ] Missing or ambiguous company information does not stop contact or deal sync.
- [ ] Axiom records created, reused and skipped counts with stable reason codes and no raw personal data.
- [ ] This ticket performs no historical mass backfill.
- [ ] Browser QA confirms the company is visible from both the contact and deal.

## Out of scope

* Historical mass company backfill.
* Fuzzy company matching.
* Automatic company merging.
* Broader enrichment and metadata UI work owned by ENG-9071.

## Blocked by

* ENG-12420 - Make Contact and Deal Updates Atomic
* ENG-12422 - Handle Uncommon CRM Stages Deterministically
* ENG-12423 - Remove Legacy CRM Model Calls
* ENG-12428 - Store and Show CRM Company Employee Ranges

relatedSnapshot.title: Add CRM enrichment fields and metadata from cold email leads
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Cold email campaign leads can contain useful saved enrichment data from Company Two SuperSearch / AI Lead Search and linked lead scrape records, but several useful company and person fields are not currently preserved or shown in the CRM.

The related issue ENG-9070 covers automatically creating and linking CRM companies from cold email campaign leads. This issue is only about preserving and exposing richer enrichment data once CRM company/contact records exist or are being created.

## Outcome

CRM company and contact records created from cold email lead enrichment retain the most useful source metadata, expose important first-class fields clearly in the API/UI, and avoid losing unmapped enrichment details.

## Scope

Add CRM company/contact enrichment support needed to preserve and show useful metadata from cold email campaign leads.

Includes:

* field mapping from persisted lead enrichment sources into CRM company/contact records
* additive data model/API/UI changes needed to store and display those fields clearly
* preservation of unmapped enrichment metadata so useful source data is not lost
* tests covering mapping, persistence, and non-destructive behavior

Does not include:

* automatic company creation/linking from campaign leads; that is covered by ENG-9070
* overwriting stronger user-entered CRM data with weaker inferred metadata
* treating person enrichment as company enrichment
* risky renaming of existing database columns unless migration/deployment risk is explicitly handled

## Source data

Use persisted campaign lead data, not just fields visible in the lead table UI.

Source priority:

1. `outreach_campaign_lead.metadata.instantlyData.payload`
2. `outreach_campaign_lead.custom_fields`
3. linked `lead_scrape_lead.raw_data` as fallback

## Saved model / behavior model

### Company fields

Update the CRM company model / API / UI as needed so the following can be stored and displayed clearly:

* `industry`
* `subIndustry` as a separate field from industry
* company website, using `crm_company.websites` if appropriate, but exposed clearly as the primary company website
* normalized company domain as a separate field
* company LinkedIn, clearly named/labeled as company-level LinkedIn
* company headcount as a range/text value when the source provides values like `1-10`, `11-50`, `201-500`, etc.

Do not force headcount ranges into the existing integer-only `employees` field. If `employees` remains in use, populate it only when a precise integer is available.

### Company metadata preservation

`crm_company` currently does not have a generic metadata JSON column. Add `crm_company.metadata jsonb` or equivalent if needed so unmapped company enrichment is not lost.

Preserve useful unmapped company enrichment such as:

* raw `companyHeadCount`
* raw headcount range/source value
* `subIndustry` if it is not otherwise stored first-class
* company enrichment source
* other company-level fields from Company Two / SuperSearch payloads that do not yet have first-class columns

### Contact metadata

Useful person-level enrichment should be preserved on `crm_contact.metadata`, which already exists.

Examples:

* `headline`
* `department`
* `jobLevel`
* person LinkedIn profile
* `linkedinConnections`, named clearly as LinkedIn connections rather than generic `connectionCount`

Do not store person fields as company fields.

## Field mapping guidance

### Company-level mappings

* Company name: `companyName`, `company_name`
* Description / summary: `companyDescription`, `summary`
* Industry: `industry`
* Sub industry: `subIndustry`
* Name 18: `companyWebsite`, `website`
* Domain: `companyDomain`, normalized website/email-derived domain where appropriate
* Company LinkedIn: company LinkedIn URL/profile fields
* Headcount range: `companyHeadCount`, headcount range fields, or equivalent source values
* Integer employees: only populate when a precise integer is available

### Person-level mappings

* Headline: `headline`
* Department: `department`
* Job level: `jobLevel`
* Person LinkedIn: person LinkedIn URL/profile fields
* LinkedIn connections: source `connectionCount`, stored with a clear key/name such as `linkedinConnections`

## Permissions / ownership

No new permissions behavior is specified here. This issue is about persistence, mapping, and presentation of enrichment data within existing CRM company/contact flows.

## UX behavior

Company fields should be shown with unambiguous labels so users can distinguish:

* industry vs sub industry
* company website vs domain
* company LinkedIn vs person LinkedIn
* headcount range vs integer employee count

The API/UI should expose the primary website clearly even if storage continues to use an existing websites collection.

## Acceptance criteria

* Industry and sub industry are both stored and displayed separately for CRM companies.
* Name 18 is stored/displayed clearly as a company website.
* Domain is stored/displayed as its own company field.
* Company LinkedIn is clearly labeled/named as company LinkedIn.
* Company headcount ranges from metadata are preserved without forcing them into integer-only employees.
* `crm_company` can preserve unmapped company enrichment metadata.
* Person metadata such as headline, department, job level, person LinkedIn, and LinkedIn connections is preserved on `crm_contact.metadata`.
* LinkedIn connection count is named clearly as LinkedIn connections, not generic connection count.
* Existing manual company/contact fields are not overwritten by weaker inferred data.
* Unit tests cover metadata mapping, field persistence, and preservation of existing user-entered data.

## Open questions or design follow-ups

* Should enrichment writes only backfill empty first-class CRM fields, or are there any cases where newer source data may update an existing inferred value?
* What should happen when multiple source locations provide conflicting values for the same field after source-priority rules are applied?
* How should the UI behave when both a precise employee count and a headcount range are available?
* Should domain be stored only as a normalized derived field, or also preserve the exact source domain string in metadata when it differs?
* Which unmapped company enrichment fields are important enough to promote to first-class columns now versus leaving in metadata?
* Are any of these newly exposed fields required in list views/search/filtering, or only on detail views for this phase?

relatedSnapshot.title: Transfer 7000 lead credits between workspaces
relatedSnapshot.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 19 & Name 20

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 21's workspace

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Consolidate this client's lead credits into a single workspace. The client (Name 19 / Name 20) has two workspaces: the Name 19 workspace and the Company Three workspace. I need roughly 7,000 lead credits moved out of the Name 19 workspace and into the Company Three workspace so all his credits sit in one place. - the latest credit purchase made by the client.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

The client purchased additional lead credits but loaded them into the Name 19 workspace by mistake. I have checked both workspaces and confirmed the \~7,000 credits are currently sitting in the Name 19 workspace.

#### What is happening instead?

The \~7,000 credits are stuck in the Name 19 workspace, split from his main Company Three workspace, with no self-serve option to transfer them. As a result the client cannot run all his leads and campaigns from one workspace.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Approximately 7,000 lead credits transferred from the Name 19 workspace into the Company Three workspace, so all of the client's credits are consolidated in JD and he can run everything from one place. If a transfer is not possible, a clear confirmation so I can set the right expectation with the client.
